title: Spectral Transformer Neural Processes
claim: A frequency-aware module converts a context set's empirical spectrum into a compact task-adaptive spectral mixture that conditions a downstream predictor.
layout: 4 panels, two rows, steps 1-4 snaking right then left, arrows between stages
description: A four-step pipeline figure on two tinted bands, blue on top and yellow below. Step 1 (top left): a context set (x_i, y_i) feeds a stack of pink frequency boxes, each with cosine and sine waveforms and small bar gauges for a_k, b_k and E_k. Step 2 (top right): a feature stack of log E_k, a_k, b_k and a frequency channel passes through a CNN responsibility network (Conv1D, Norm, GELU, Conv1D, Softmax). The output is a blue heatmap of soft assignments over Q=6 components. A black arrow runs down to Step 3 (bottom right), which shows a stem plot of the discrete spectrum overlaid with Gaussian mixture curves, a legend of weights, means and sigmas, and a yellow box of compression equations. Step 4 (bottom left) shows sampled frequencies per component as diamonds on a Q-versus-omega axis. Below it are the embedding formulas. Arrows lead to a concatenate block, then the TNP block, then a small Gaussian output with mu and sigma.
caption: Overview of STNPs. (a) An empirical spectrum is estimated from the context set on a fixed frequency grid via cosine/sine projections of centred responses. (b) A CNN responsibility network softly assigns each grid frequency to one of \(Q\) mixture components. (c) The discrete spectrum is compressed into a Gaussian mixture with weights, means, and variances induced by the responsibilities. (d) Task-adaptive frequencies sampled from this mixture form spectral embeddings, which are concatenated with the MLP token representation and passed to the TNP predictor.
abstract: Time series, spatial data, and images are natural applications of Neural Processes. However, when such data exhibit strong periodicity and quasi-periodicity, existing methods often suffer from underfitting and generalise poorly beyond the training distribution. In this work, we propose Spectral Transformer Neural Processes (STNPs), a frequency-aware extension of Transformer Neural Processes (TNPs). STNPs introduce a Spectral Aggregator that estimates an empirical context spectrum, compresses it into a spectral mixture, samples task-adaptive spectral features, and concatenates them with time-domain embeddings, thereby injecting a spectral-mixture-kernel bias into TNPs. This design reshapes the similarity geometry, allowing inputs that are distant in Euclidean space to remain close in an induced periodic manifold while enhancing time-frequency interactions. Extensive experiments on synthetic regression tasks, real-world time-series datasets, and an image dataset demonstrate that STNPs consistently improve predictive performance over existing baselines, extending Neural Processes beyond translation equivariance towards effective modelling of periodicity and quasi-periodicity.
